_what: Level 1 of the Operating Procedures manual. Stages follow the playbook map in docs/PLAYBOOKS.md (the listing, the buyer, leads, every day), with the listing split into its steps. Every statement carries its source; build_site.py computes each stage's agents from identity/playbooks.json.

story.t: A web form arrives. It goes to the dispatcher (Agent 00), not to an agent. The dispatcher checks that an inquiry from outside to Agent 01 is on the track, numbers it for this client, writes it to the record, and delivers it to Agent 01.
Agent 01 records the inquiry and the consent, then asks Agent 14 whether the person is already on record. That question also goes through the dispatcher: checked, numbered, recorded, delivered.
Agent 14 answers, again through the dispatcher: not a duplicate.
Agent 01 hands the lead to Agent 02, which scores it on the authorized user's rubric: warm. It goes to Agent 03.
Agent 03 sends the sequence's text to Compliance (Agent 17), which returns its verdict, each through the dispatcher.

A route that is not on the track would have been refused, and a message of a kind that is on no route at all would have been held with a question for the authorized user. A message to a vendor or the public would have been held for the authorized user's release.

system.t: Each inquiry is captured with its consent, checked against the record, scored on the signed rubric and routed: hot to the authorized user, warm to follow-up sequences the authorized user wrote, cold archived with the reason. Warm leads are re-scored every 7 days. Prospects from a discovery feed are passed to the authorized user; the system has no route to contact them.

person.t: Calling a hot lead.
Writing the scoring rubric and the follow-up sequences.
person.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_02.py::missing = REQUIRED_RUBRIC_KEYS - set(new_rubric.keys()); dispatcher/listing_spokes_03.py::if env.intent == "config.update" and "nurture_sequences" in env.payload:

person.t: Every decision to contact a prospect.
Signing any farm campaign.

system.t: Agent 10 assembles the comparable sales the authorized user supplies, keeping only figures with a source and date (and, when the request gives today's date, none older than 30 days), with no opinion.

person.t: The price opinion and the list price.
The listing agreement with the seller (outside the system).
person.src: identity/routes.json (no route carries a listing agreement)

system.t: The signed listing package starts it. Photography is booked from the approved roster (the booking waits for release), the description is built from the property data and checked by Compliance, the listing is set active as the package allows, and its publication waits for the authorized user's release.

person.t: Signing the listing package and price.
Releasing the photographer's booking and each publication.

system.t: Showings are confirmed only with the buyer agreement on file and the calendar's say (a showing the calendar did not take is confirmed only if the authorized user continues it). The weekly seller report counts showings and feedback and waits for the authorized user. For a price conversation the system assembles the comparables it is given and never a number; a price changes only on the authorized user's signature. A vacant listing gets a property check ordered on each daily run (the booking waits for release). Access grants are recorded without a code named in them (a value naming the code, combination, PIN or password is rejected). A withdrawn or expired listing stops its marketing.

person.t: Every price change.
Releasing each weekly seller report.
Granting and closing property access.
Talking with the seller about price.

system.t: Criteria are kept as signed and matched against new listings; matches wait until the written buyer agreement is on file. Showings are booked through Agent 06; criteria change only from the buyer's explicit feedback or the authorized user's signed criteria.

person.t: The buyer agreement.
Recording the buyer's criteria.
Every price, seller-position and neighborhood question.

system.t: The authorized user records each offer status; it goes to the authorized user's queue and is logged, never to a client.

person.t: Writing, presenting and negotiating every offer (outside the system).

system.t: The listing goes pending on the authorized user's signature. The contract's dates, signed by the authorized user, become the timeline; a date changes only by a signed amendment. Documents are requested, checked (sensitive ones only from listed senders) and filed; a milestone counts as met with its document (an inspection report or appraisal counts whatever it says) or the authorized user's waiver at closing, and the close is held while any is open.

person.t: The contract and its dates.

Repair, appraisal, title and earnest-money matters (a legal-line alert when repairs are requested or not stated, an appraisal is below the price, a title exception is found, or earnest money is not confirmed).
Every wire and money matter.

system.t: The commission is recorded and the 30, 90 and 365-day check-ins are scheduled for people on the authorized user's list. Every touch stops for an opt-out, a hard time on record or a contact that no longer works. A complaint holds routine messages to that person until the authorized user lifts the hold.

person.t: Every response to a complaint.
Whether to reach out during a hard time.
Any answer about a referral reward.

system.t: The morning briefing is built from the record: calendar, waiting items, decisions waiting, new leads, record conflicts, yesterday's figures, prospects waiting, listing changes received and compliance notices. The evening run sends Agent 14's counts (over every record it holds) and the day's figures as one report. Both run only when started: the daily run from the Desk, run_sweeps.py or a scheduler the office sets up; the evening run from run_sweeps.py --evening or a scheduler.

person.t: Reading the briefing and setting priorities.
Starting the daily and evening runs, or scheduling them.

always_person.t: Price: every list price and price change. The system records a signed price and offers no opinion.
Negotiation and offers: recorded as statuses only.
Advice: a request for advice raises a legal-line alert.
Money: the system has no route that moves money.
Anything to a vendor, the other side or the public: held until the authorized user releases that message.
A situation no rule covers: the agent holds it and asks.
